requirements.evidence: CallMode enum with any/priority_only/normal_only (app/Enums/CallMode.php:5-9); NoWaitingTicketsException extends RuntimeException (app/Exceptions/NoWaitingTicketsException.php:8); invokable signature matches contract (app/Actions/CallNextTicket.php:19); queue re-read + lock inside the transaction and inactive rejection (app/Actions/CallNextTicket.php:23-26); deterministic ordering with priority/issued_at/id (app/Actions/CallNextTicket.php:58,66); fairness limited to any mode using the last 3 called by called_at desc, id desc and a waiting-normal check (app/Actions/CallNextTicket.php:31-48); per-candidate lock + waiting re-check before writing only status/called_at/called_by_user_id (app/Actions/CallNextTicket.php:71-83); dedicated exception when nothing is eligible (app/Actions/CallNextTicket.php:86).

conventions.evidence: Domain write correctly lives in app/Actions/CallNextTicket.php (conventions.md:42-45) and the docs were touched (docs/business-rules.md:133, docs/architecture.md:103), but the change ships no test at all, breaking the mandatory test-first rule (conventions.md:12-21) and the CHANGELOG requirement (conventions.md:103).

security.evidence: Task explicitly puts authorization out of scope and the caller is trusted (task.md:11-12,64-67), so no policy is expected; no unvalidated user input, direct attribute writes instead of mass assignment (app/Actions/CallNextTicket.php:81-83), no output/Blade changes, and the queue-row lock plus candidate re-lock prevent the double-call race (app/Actions/CallNextTicket.php:23,73).

tests.evidence: change.diff contains only app/Actions/CallNextTicket.php, app/Enums/CallMode.php, app/Exceptions/NoWaitingTicketsException.php and two docs files; there is no tests/ file and no test added for ordering, fairness, modes, exceptions or the concurrent-call re-check.

simplicity.evidence: Lean single action reusing the existing Query Exception/Queue/Ticket APIs, one ordered query per mode (app/Actions/CallNextTicket.php:58-74); only excess is `return $candidate->fresh();` after a save that already leaves the model up to date (app/Actions/CallNextTicket.php:81-87) and an extra query (`$hasNormal`) computed only inside any mode.

readability.evidence: Short focused methods, explanatory comments (app/Actions/CallNextTicket.php:22-24,28,34,57,76) and clear mode switch; nits: `$priorityStreak` actually counts priority tickets among the last three rather than a streak (app/Actions/CallNextTicket.php:39) and docs/architecture.md:104-105 adds two blank lines plus a non-ASCII hyphen.

scope.evidence: Five files, all serving the task: the action, its enum, its exception and the two docs the task names (task.md:50-51); no refactors, no unrelated features.

issues.explanation: No Pest/PHPUnit test is added for any of the new behaviour (ordering, each mode, fairness streak, inactive-queue rejection, empty-queue exception, concurrent re-check), so the fairness and exactly-once logic is entirely unverified.
The change breaks the project's mandatory test-first rule by shipping production code with no accompanying test.
Conventions require an entry under [Unreleased] for every change, and the CHANGELOG was not updated.
The required architecture update is a single generic sentence that does not describe the modes, ordering or fairness rule it is supposed to document.
`$priorityStreak` names a count of priority tickets among the last three calls, not a streak; a name like `$priorityCount` would read truer.
`return $candidate->fresh();` issues an extra query for a model that was just saved with all three changed attributes already set; returning `$candidate` would do.
The edit leaves two consecutive blank lines and uses a non-breaking hyphen in "queue‑level", both inconsistent with the surrounding markdown.

review.summary: The change adds the CallMode enum, NoWaitingTicketsException and a CallNextTicket action that locks the queue, applies the deterministic ordering and the 3-priority-call fairness rule, then locks and re-checks the chosen ticket before writing only the call fields and updating the two requested docs. The domain logic reads as a correct implementation of the task, but the change ships with zero tests, which violates the project's non-negotiable test-first convention for exactly the fairness and concurrency logic most in need of coverage, so it needs changes before merging. Smaller gaps are the missing CHANGELOG entry and a very thin architecture description.
